A new model of decentralized cardiovascular research is taking shape Pts can be identified through clinical records, contacted directly, and enrolled remotely, testing arranged at local labs-->brings selected research activities closer to where people live Participation more manageable around work, travel and family responsibilities (more practical) In American Journal of Preventive Cardiology sim pub with American Heart Association #AHA26 presentation Mitsuaki Sawano Harlan Krumholz Yuan Lu put this approach into practice through UNRAVEL, studying Lp(a) in adults with ASCVD across the nation https://lnkd.in/g-QBhG5d >20K individuals contacted, of >2K prescreening respondents, 922 enrolled participants in record time (13 months), lab completion rate 99.5%, 82% rated their overall experience as 9-10 out of 10. Amazing #'s. We dont see these in conventional research designs! In my accompanying editorial, “Knocking on New Doors: UNRAVELing the Future of Decentralized Cardiovascular Research” https://lnkd.in/gy88SJeT I discuss what it will take for this model to fulfill its promise 1. 90% of participants came from Connecticut. Making enrollment available remotely does not ensure that we reach different communities will require local clinicians, community organizations and people whom potential participants trust. 2. decentralized testing needs a clear connection back to care. Need to build direct connections to clinicians and measure what happens after testing. Participants should not have to carry that coordination alone. 3. Future studies should account cost considerations vs conventional approaches. 4. Next phase should bring multiple health systems together around common eligibility, coordinated oversight and shared outcomes. Each would recruit through its own clinical and community relationships. This could combine consistent scientific methods with wider local participation. Take home message? Biggest opportunity is to build research that fits more naturally into people’s lives, reaches a broader population, and connects discovery with care. Congratulations to Yale School of Medicine entire team for giving us a credible starting point. A new future of clinical studies is knocking at our door. We need to ensure that we are not simply knocking on the same doors American Society for Preventive Cardiology (ASPC)
